classification: RECOMMENDATION throughout, except where marked CURRENT_FACT.
status: DESIGN PROPOSAL. No aggregate below exists in source. Nothing is implemented by this artifact.

bounded_context.name: Creative Marketplace
bounded_context.source: AGENTS.md sections 1, 2 and 8 declare Creative as a bounded domain inside Project 01, initialised as a capability, with Project 03 CMS as a separate application and database.
bounded_context.current_state: CURRENT_FACT — not implemented. 0 classes, 0 tables, 0 routes, 0 migrations, 0 tests. app/Domain/Creative, app/Services/Creative, app/Repositories/Creative and app/Http/Controllers/Creative are all absent from disk.
bounded_context.boundary_rule: A class belongs to Creative if and only if its reason to change is a Creative Marketplace business rule. A class belongs to a shared capability if it changes for a non-Creative reason.
bounded_context.ubiquitous_language_warning: CURRENT_FACT — 'asset' in this repository means AD INVENTORY (a Screen), not creative work. 'review' means an admin approving an uploaded ad asset. 'media' means the file a client uploads for a booking. 'service' means a MediaService/MailContractInterface, not a purchasable creative service. Creative must not adopt any of these four words for a domain concept without an explicit naming decision.

aggregates.purpose: Identity, capability and commercial standing of a person or studio that supplies creative work.
aggregates.lifecycle_note: OPEN DECISION. The vocabulary and the suspension/deactivation split are not defined by any project document. The closest precedent is screen_providers: draft, pending_review (DB default), approved, rejected, inactive.

value_objects.name: CreatorSlug
value_objects.note: See open decision on public identifier strategy

value_objects.name: Craft
value_objects.purpose: The category of creative work a creator supplies
value_objects.note: OPEN DECISION: free-form vs enumerated vs taxonomy table

value_objects.name: PayoutDetails
value_objects.note: OPEN DECISION: no equivalent exists anywhere in the repository. Any storage of payout details is a new compliance surface.

entities.name: CreatorProfile
entities.note: One-to-one with Creator; bio, headline, capabilities

entities.name: PortfolioItem
entities.note: A portfolio entry; references stored files, not an embedded blob

aggregates.relationships: Creator 1..1 User (via users.id). Creator 1..N CreativeService. Creator 1..N PortfolioItem. Creator 1..N CreativeProposal. Creator 1..N CreatorEarning. Creator 1..N CreatorPayout.
aggregates.who_can_mutate: Creator for profile/portfolio/availability (own only). Admin for status transitions and verification. Nobody else.
aggregates.authorization_boundary: Route middleware 'permission:creative.creators.*' for admin actions; a new CreatorPolicy for ownership actions. This is NEW WORK — the repository has no policy layer.
aggregates.financial_boundary: A Creator does not hold money. Earnings are a separate aggregate precisely so a creator's commercial standing and their balance are not the same object.
reuse_from_marketplace: users.id as the identity anchor (DIRECT)
role/permission machinery (EXTEND vocabulary)
StorageContractInterface for avatars and portfolio images (DIRECT)
ActivityLog for transitions (DIRECT)
aggregates.must_be_new: Everything else — table, model, domain rules, repository, service, policy, requests, resources, events.

aggregates.purpose: A listing by which a creator offers a defined unit of creative work at a defined rate.
aggregates.lifecycle_note: RECOMMENDATION. The published/paused split is what makes discovery safe; the existing screen_categories.status (active/inactive) and blogs.status (draft/published) are the in-repo precedents.

value_objects.name: Rate
value_objects.purpose: Price + currency + pricing unit (per project / per hour / per item / per day)
value_objects.note: OPEN DECISION: is a rate mandatory, or can a service be 'quote on request'? This determines whether the Brief can be priced at creation.

value_objects.name: DeliveryCommitment
value_objects.purpose: Turnaround time and included revision count
value_objects.note: OPEN DECISION: revision count is a commercial term and belongs on the accepted proposal, not only the listing.

aggregates.relationships: CreativeService N..1 Creator. CreativeService N..1 CreativeServiceCategory (via junction). CreativeService 1..N PortfolioItem (optional linkage).
aggregates.authorization_boundary: permission:creative.services.* for admin; CreativeServicePolicy for the owner.
aggregates.financial_boundary: A published rate is a price quote, not a financial fact. A financial fact is created only when a proposal is accepted.
reuse_from_marketplace: SettingsService for a platform-wide minimum/maximum and a default rate policy (DIRECT)
ExchangeRateService for displaying a foreign-currency rate (DIRECT)
StorageContractInterface for cover images (DIRECT)
aggregates.must_be_new: Everything else. IMPORTANT: do NOT reuse pricing_plans, PricingService or PricingRuleEngine. Those price advertising media time with duration/peak/weekend/screen-count rules. A creative service rate is a different money model.

aggregates.purpose: A client's statement of work: what is needed, with what constraints, by when, with what budget expectation.
aggregates.lifecycle: draft -> open (published to creators) -> in_proposal (proposals received) -> awarded -> closed
aggregates.lifecycle_note: OPEN DECISION. Whether a brief is a standalone object that creators browse, or is always created against a specific CreativeService (and therefore a specific creator), is not determined by any project document. The two models produce different schemas.

value_objects.name: Scope
value_objects.note: OPEN DECISION: free text, structured line items, or both. Structured line items are needed if a brief is priced automatically; free text is needed if it is quote-on-request.

value_objects.name: BudgetRange
value_objects.purpose: Optional min/max expectation in a currency
value_objects.note: OPEN DECISION: whether a budget is mandatory, optional, or forbidden. Publishing a budget changes proposal dynamics completely.

entities.name: BriefAttachment
entities.note: References a private stored file; never a public path

aggregates.relationships: CreativeBrief N..1 User (the client). CreativeBrief 0..1 N..1 CreativeService. CreativeBrief 1..N CreativeProposal.
important_states: closes_at (OPEN DECISION: does a brief expire?)
aggregates.who_can_mutate: Owning client; admin; a creator may not mutate a brief (a proposal is the creator's response, not an edit to the brief).
aggregates.authorization_boundary: CreativeBriefPolicy (own client only). Public discovery must use a read model that does not expose the client's identity.
aggregates.financial_boundary: A brief's budget is an expectation, never a financial fact. No payment may reference a brief.
reuse_from_marketplace: StorageContractInterface via a NEW private-disk adapter for attachments
rate limiting on creation (EXTEND)
ActivityLog for transitions (DIRECT)

aggregates.purpose: A creator's offer to fulfil a brief: price, timeline, scope, included revisions.
aggregates.lifecycle_note: OPEN DECISION. Two unresolved questions: (a) may a brief receive multiple proposals, or exactly one? (b) is acceptance exclusive, i.e. does accepting one proposal auto-decline the others? Both change the concurrency design.

value_objects.name: QuotedAmount
value_objects.note: CRITICAL OPEN DECISION. See 'server-derived amounts' in the decision register.

value_objects.name: Timeline
value_objects.note: OPEN DECISION: fixed dates or a duration in working days

aggregates.relationships: CreativeProposal N..1 CreativeBrief. CreativeProposal N..1 Creator. Accepted CreativeProposal 1..1 CreativeProject.
aggregates.authorization_boundary: CreativeProposalPolicy. The client must be the brief's owner, not merely any authenticated user.
aggregates.financial_boundary: The accepted proposal's amount becomes a frozen financial fact, snapshotted onto the CreativeProject.
reuse_from_marketplace: NONE of the existing proposal machinery — there is none. A proposal is a first-class new concept.
aggregates.must_be_new: Everything. THIS IS THE FIRST CONCURRENCY-CRITICAL AGGREGATE IN CREATIVE: acceptance must be exactly-once (see 16-transaction-concurrency-analysis.json).

aggregates.purpose: The engagement created when a proposal is accepted. Owns the agreed commercial terms and the work lifecycle.
aggregates.lifecycle: funded_pending -> awaiting_start -> in_progress -> in_review -> delivered -> completed | cancelled
aggregates.lifecycle_note: RECOMMENDATION, modelled on the in-repo booking state graph (App\Services\BookingWorkflowService:14-39) which is the only existing multi-state machine. OPEN DECISION: whether funding precedes or follows project creation, and whether 'delivered' and 'completed' are distinct (delivered = creator submitted, completed = client accepted).

value_objects.name: AgreedTerms
value_objects.purpose: frozen snapshot: quoted amount, currency, commission rate, platform fee, creator net, delivery date, included revisions
value_objects.note: MUST be immutable once the project is created, mirroring bookings.pricing_snapshot and booking_screens revenue columns.

entities.name: CreativeProjectItem
entities.note: A line item of the agreed scope. If a proposal is a single lump sum, this table is NOT REQUIRED — see 09-creative-database-target-schema-blueprint.json.

aggregates.relationships: CreativeProject 1..1 accepted CreativeProposal. CreativeProject N..1 CreativeBrief. CreativeProject N..1 Creator. CreativeProject 1..1..N CreativeRevision. CreativeProject 1..1..N CreativeDelivery. CreativeProject 0..1 CreativeReview. CreativeProject 0..N CreatorEarning.
aggregates.who_can_mutate: Creator and client, each limited to their own transitions. Admin may cancel. Finance/admin for funding and payout actions.
aggregates.authorization_boundary: CreativeProjectPolicy — both the client (brief owner) and the creator are authorised actors, with different allowed transitions per role. This is a new authorization shape: no existing aggregate has two parties with asymmetric transition rights.
aggregates.financial_boundary: AgreedTerms is the boundary between the Creative domain and the shared financial infrastructure. Earnings are created only from AgreedTerms, never recomputed.
reuse_from_marketplace: The state-machine PATTERN from App\Services\BookingWorkflowService (not the class).
The immutable-snapshot PATTERN from bookings.pricing_snapshot and booking_pricing_breakdowns.
payment gateway via PaymentGatewayInterface (contract only).
aggregates.must_be_new: Everything else. DO NOT reuse InventoryService, ConflictDetectionService, BookingCapacityService or ManualBookingService — they are all hard-wired to Screen rows and booking overlap windows.

aggregates.purpose: A requested change to a delivered item and the creator's response to it, forming an auditable round.
aggregates.lifecycle_note: OPEN DECISION — the most consequential unresolved product question. Specifically: how many revision rounds are included (is the limit in AgreedTerms?), does an over-limit request require a paid change order, and who decides when the limit is reached?
aggregates.relationships: CreativeRevision N..1 CreativeProject. CreativeRevision N..1 CreativeDelivery (the item being revised) — OPEN DECISION: is a revision always against a specific delivery, or against the project? Against a delivery is safer for auditability.
aggregates.who_can_mutate: Client requests; creator submits; client accepts or rejects.
aggregates.financial_boundary: An over-limit revision may create an additional earning. That is a financial consequence and requires a decided pricing rule (OPEN DECISION).
reuse_from_marketplace: NOTHING. grep -ri 'revision' = 0 matches in the repository. This concept is entirely new.
The approval PATTERN from booking_media review (review_status + reviewed_by + reviewed_at + rejection_reason) is a reasonable shape template.

aggregates.purpose: A submission of work by the creator for client acceptance.
aggregates.lifecycle_note: OPEN DECISION: on rejection, does the delivery become 'superseded' and a new delivery is created, or is it revised in place? 'Superseded' (append-only) is strongly recommended for auditability and matches the immutability discipline in AGENTS.md section 10.

value_objects.name: DeliveryManifest
value_objects.purpose: what was delivered, in what form

aggregates.relationships: CreativeDelivery N..1 CreativeProject. CreativeDelivery 1..N DeliveredFile. CreativeDelivery 0..N CreativeRevision.
aggregates.who_can_mutate: Creator submits; client reviews. Admin may intervene.
aggregates.authorization_boundary: CreativeDeliveryPolicy. File download must additionally be authorised per file, not per delivery row — see 19-creative-security-risk-register.json (SR-05).
aggregates.financial_boundary: Acceptance of a delivery may trigger earning creation. The trigger rule is an OPEN DECISION (on delivery acceptance vs on project completion vs on settlement period).
reuse_from_marketplace: StorageContractInterface — but see the private-disk requirement. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-SECURITY-SENSITIVE REUSE POINT IN THE ENTIRE CREATIVE BUILD.
MediaConfig-style extension allowlists (EXTEND with a creative.* group)
aggregates.must_be_new: Everything else. DO NOT route Creative uploads through App\Http\Controllers\FileController: it has zero validation, uses the client-supplied $request->path as the storage directory, and preserves the client-supplied extension.

aggregates.purpose: The client's structured assessment of a completed engagement.
aggregates.lifecycle_note: RECOMMENDATION — a review is written once and is immutable. There is no review state machine. OPEN DECISION: is a review required for a project to complete, or optional? Is it one per project or one per delivery? Is it public on the creator's profile?

value_objects.name: Rating
value_objects.note: testimonials.rating is decimal(3,2) validated min:0|max:5 and is NOT cast on the model. Creative should use a small unsigned integer and validate explicitly. OPEN DECISION: single overall rating, or per-criterion scores?

aggregates.relationships: CreativeReview N..1 CreativeProject. N..1 Creator (denormalised for the profile read model). N..1 User (the reviewer, who is the client).
important_states: none — immutability replaces the state machine
aggregates.who_can_mutate: The client, once, and only if they were a party to the project. Nobody may edit or delete a review.
aggregates.authorization_boundary: CreativeReviewPolicy + a strict one-per-project-per-reviewer unique constraint.
aggregates.financial_boundary: A rating may affect future ranking or commission tiering. OPEN DECISION — if it affects money, then a review can never be edited, which reinforces immutability.
reuse_from_marketplace: NOTHING. testimonials.rating is public marketing content with no author binding; reusing it would let anyone edit any rating.

aggregates.purpose: An immutable financial fact: an amount earned by a creator from a specific project, under specific terms.
aggregates.owner: CREATIVE domain for accrual; SHARED financial infrastructure for settlement and payout.
aggregates.lifecycle_note: OPEN DECISION — this is the most under-specified area in the entire brief. Unanswered: (a) when does an earning accrue — delivery accepted, project completed, review submitted, or after a dispute window? (b) is there a dispute/hold window at all? (c) who approves an earning? (d) is the creator paid automatically or on request? (e) what is the platform commission basis — the quoted amount, or the amount net of fees?

value_objects.name: EarningAmount
value_objects.purpose: gross, platform commission, creator net — computed once, stored, never recomputed
value_objects.note: MUST mirror the booking_screens pattern (gross_revenue, platform_share, provider_share + the split percentages) so the split is auditable.

value_objects.name: SettlementPeriod
value_objects.purpose: the window in which an earning becomes payable

aggregates.relationships: CreatorEarning N..1 CreativeProject. N..1 Creator. N..0..1 settlement batch. N..0..N CreatorPayout line.
aggregates.who_can_mutate: System (accrual, from a project event). Finance/admin (approve, release). Creator may REQUEST a payout but never approve their own earning.
aggregates.authorization_boundary: permission:creative.earnings.view for the creator's own; permission:creative.payouts.approve for finance. Separation of duties between request and approve is MANDATORY.
aggregates.financial_boundary: THE CENTRAL BOUNDARY OF THE WHOLE CREATIVE BUILD. See section 'Financial boundary analysis' below.
reuse_from_marketplace: The PATTERN from partner_commissions (state lifecycle + immutable profit snapshot) and screen_provider_settlements (period + release).
Money conversion from App\Domain\Payment\Support\Money for the gateway only.
The payment gateway for actual disbursement, via PaymentGatewayInterface.
aggregates.must_be_new: The earning aggregate, the creator balance derivation, and the payout request flow. DECISION REQUIRED on whether to extract CommissionService/SettlementService into shared contracts or build Creative equivalents.

domain_services.name: ProposalSelectionDomainService
domain_services.responsibility: Decides which proposal is valid to accept for a given brief and rejects invalid ones (expired, withdrawn, budget-mismatched, creator-suspended).

domain_services.name: EarningsCalculationDomainService
domain_services.responsibility: Computes gross, platform commission and creator net from a frozen AgreedTerms snapshot. Pure, deterministic, no I/O. This is the direct analogue of App\Domain\Financial\Support\RevenueAllocation::split, which is the ONLY existing pure financial function in the repository and is therefore the correct template.

domain_services.name: RevisionEntitlementDomainService
domain_services.responsibility: Decides whether a requested revision is within the agreed included rounds and computes any over-limit charge.

domain_services.name: CreatorEligibilityDomainService
domain_services.responsibility: Decides whether a creator may receive work (status, verification, availability).

domain_events.name: CreatorRegistered
domain_events.existing_precedent: UserRegistered (App\Support\Events\Notifications\UserRegistered) — same shape, add a Creative consumer

domain_events.name: ProposalAccepted
domain_events.existing_precedent: NONE. Closest shape is BookingApproved — and the most important one, because acceptance is the financial commitment point

domain_event_note: RECOMMENDATION: all 13 events should be emitted AFTER the transaction commits, not inside it. CURRENT_FACT: no existing event implements ShouldHandleEventsAfterCommit; the current pattern dispatches inside the transaction (ManualBookingService:642), which can notify for a rolled-back write. Creative should not inherit that.

integration_events.name: CreativeProjectCompleted (integration)
integration_events.purpose: Notify Project 03 CMS / analytics that a creative engagement completed
integration_events.note: Must be a separate event from the domain event, per the CMS boundary in AGENTS.md section 9 (versioned APIs, events, webhooks, external IDs).

state_machines_summary.no_existing_pattern: No aggregate in this repository has TWO parties with asymmetric transition rights on the same object. CreativeProject (client + creator) and CreativeProposal (creator submits, client accepts) are the first. There is no template to copy; this must be designed from first principles.

financial_boundary_analysis.question: Should creator earnings reuse the existing settlement infrastructure?

hard_coupling_points: SettlementService imports 7 models including Booking, BookingScreen and Screen
CommissionService locks partner_commissions then referral_usages in that order
RevenueSplitResolverService has 5 split sources, none of them creator-related

reusable_with_new_implementation: Commission lifecycle machinery — extract a contract OR reimplement
Settlement period release — new eligibility predicate OR immediate release

financial_boundary_analysis.recommendation: RECOMMENDATION: Do NOT extend screen_provider_settlements or partner_commissions with creator columns. Create creator_earnings and creator_payouts as separate aggregates, and extract ONLY the lifecycle pattern (state + transition guard + pessimistic lock) into a shared contract if and only if both domains need it. The existing settlement and commission services are too tightly coupled to advertising to be generalised without a refactor that AGENTS.md section 19 forbids performing opportunistically.
financial_boundary_analysis.open_decision: OPEN DECISION: earning release trigger (delivery accepted / project completed / review submitted / after a dispute window), approval authority, dispute window existence, payout cadence, and whether the platform commission is on the quoted amount or on the net.

aggregate_count_summary.note: The declared subdomain list in AGENTS.md section 8 (Creator, Service, Brief, Proposal, Project, Revision, Delivery, Review, Earnings) is confirmed as a sound aggregate set for the initial scope. It may need extending with Disputes, Contracts, Payouts and Notifications if the product scope includes them — those are OPEN DECISIONS, not omissions.
